speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the consultation. I am Dr. Agent; to begin our assessment of your seizures and lethargy, when exactly did these symptoms first start, and have you noticed any fever or jaundice? Additionally, have you or anyone around you had a recent infection or seizures?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Sepsis (likely Group B Streptococcus or E. coli) secondary to antenatal chorioamnionitis.

Based on the history of chorioamnionitis, low birth weight, and poor Apgar scores, I am highly suspicious of neonatal sepsis manifesting as septic encephalopathy. I need to confirm this immediately with a septic workup.

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, Blood Culture, CSF Analysis, Blood Glucose, Electrolytes, and Coagulation Profile.
